text: The UN human rights office found in 2022 that serious human rights violations had been committed against Uyghurs and other mostly Muslim communities in Xinjiang, including large-scale arbitrary detention that may amount to crimes against humanity; Sheffield Hallam University's Driving Force report lists GAC Group and GAC Passenger Vehicle among the automakers operating in the Ürümqi (Toutunhe) automotive manufacturing zone in the Uyghur Region.
short: UN OHCHR found serious human-rights violations in Xinjiang; Sheffield Hallam lists GAC plants in the Ürümqi automotive zone.

source.name: UN OHCHR: OHCHR Assessment of human rights concerns in the Xinjiang Uyghur Autonomous Region, People's Republic of China
source.quote: Serious human rights violations have been committed in XUAR in the context of the Government’s application of counter-terrorism and counter-“extremism” strategies.

additionalSources.name: Sheffield Hallam University Helena Kennedy Centre & NomoGaia: Driving Force - Automotive Supply Chains and Forced Labor in the Uyghur Region (December 2022, rev. October 2024), Supply Chain Risk chapter
additionalSources.quote: Companies located in the park include Volkswagen’s Ürümchi manufacturing base (see Volkswagen text box in this chapter), and Chinese companies CRCC, CRRC, GAC Group, and Jiangsu Jinsheng.
additionalSources.note: The same passage lists GAC Passenger Vehicle Ltd Co among the parts manufacturers and recyclers in the region. This claim is about the Chinese state's Xinjiang record, not about GAC's own conduct: the report does not document labour transfers at GAC's own plants.
